plants.about: Needs some winter chill and a pollination partner nearby. Thinning now gives you fewer but bigger, sweeter apples.
plants.name: Apple
plants.next: Summer prune of long upright shoots in February.
plants.petNote: Fruit is fine, but seeds, leaves and stems are toxic. No apple seeds for the cockatiels.
plants.watch: Codling moth (holes with brown frass) and black spot on the leaves.

plants.about: Rosettes of strappy, lime-green leaves, freshly planted in bark mulch. Each rosette flowers once, then makes pups around its base.
plants.feed: Weak liquid feed monthly in summer
plants.name: Bromeliads
plants.next: Send close-up photos to confirm the type.
plants.petNote: Safe for all your pets.
plants.spot: New front bed by the fence (about 8)
plants.watch: Bleached, yellow leaves from too much afternoon sun.
plants.water: Keep the centre cup topped up

plants.about: A hybrid tea: one big, ruffled bloom per stem. It repeat-flowers all summer if you keep cutting off the spent flowers.
plants.name: Coral rose
plants.next: Deadhead after each flush of blooms.
plants.petNote: Safe, apart from the thorns. Keep pets inside while any spray dries.
plants.watch: Black spot: dark spots and yellow leaves, already showing in your photo. Also aphids on buds.

plants.about: Aromatic leaflets for curries, best picked fresh. It dislikes cold, so Auckland's sheltered spots suit it.
plants.name: Curry leaf trees
plants.next: Pinch tips to keep it bushy and leafy.
plants.petNote: Safe; the leaves are edible.
plants.spot: Back corner by the fence, and end of the side bed (2)
plants.watch: Scale and citrus psyllids on new growth; leaf drop in cold snaps.
plants.water: Weekly; don't let it dry out

plants.about: Your nursery: jelly beans, echeveria, blue chalk sticks and more, all rooting in bark mix. Most root within 3–6 weeks.
plants.name: Cuttings
plants.next: Pot up once a gentle tug meets resistance.
plants.petNote: A mixed bag: some succulents (jade, kalanchoe types) upset pets. Keep the table out of reach.
plants.spot: Table by the side fence (~19 pots)
plants.watch: Rot at the base, and sunburn on new leaves.

plants.about: Striped, strappy leaves in green and cream. It prefers shade: strong sun scorches and bleaches the stripes.
plants.name: Corn plant
plants.next: Find it a shadier home before summer.
plants.petNote: Can cause vomiting, especially in cats.
plants.spot: On the heat pump unit (move it)
plants.watch: Brown, crispy leaves from the heat pump blast and hot sun.

plants.about: A Kiwi favourite with silver-backed leaves. The red-and-white petals are edible, and ripe fruit simply drops to the ground.
plants.name: Feijoa
plants.next: Hang a guava moth trap in December.
plants.petNote: Believed safe for all your pets.
plants.watch: Guava moth grubs inside the fruit.

plants.about: Small succulents tucked between the bromeliads: blue chalk sticks, echeveria rosettes and a grey kalanchoe type. They'll spread to fill the gaps.
plants.name: Front-bed succulents
plants.next: Fill gaps with more cuttings as they root.
plants.petNote: Mixed: blue chalk sticks and kalanchoe types can upset pets if chewed.
plants.spot: New front bed by the fence
plants.watch: One near the front is yellow and shrivelled: check it isn't sitting wet or scorched.
plants.water: Only when the bark is dry underneath

plants.about: About ten palms in pots and crates under the shade cloth: golden cane, kentia and young seedlings. They love the filtered light.
plants.name: Shade-house palms
plants.next: Pot up into bigger containers in spring.
plants.petNote: Safe for all your pets.
plants.watch: One palm is yellowing all over (hungry) and one has dead brown fronds (dry or sun-scorched).

plants.about: Big mophead blooms in pink, red and white. Flower colour follows the soil: alkaline keeps pinks pink, acid turns them blue.
plants.name: Hydrangeas
plants.next: Cut off faded blooms in late summer.
plants.petNote: Can cause vomiting and an upset stomach if chewed.
plants.spot: Round stand, back corner and back fence (pink, red, white, green)
plants.watch: Wilting on hot afternoons; move pots into shade.

plants.about: A succulent with glossy, daisy-like flowers that open in the sun and close at night or on cloudy days.
plants.name: Ice plant
plants.next: Trim back after flowering to keep it compact.
plants.petNote: Generally safe.
plants.watch: Overwatering: soft, mushy stems.

plants.about: The “money tree”. It stores water in its fat leaves, and red leaf edges mean it is getting lovely sun.
plants.name: Jade plant
plants.next: Top the pot with grit once the weeds are out.
plants.petNote: Can cause vomiting and tiredness in cats and the dog.
plants.watch: Mealybugs (white fluff) and rot from wet soil.

plants.about: French lavender, with little “rabbit ear” tufts on each flower. Loves heat, and hates sitting in wet soil.
plants.name: Lavender
plants.next: Light all-over trim once flowering finishes.
plants.petNote: Mild. Only a problem if a cat chews a lot of it.
plants.watch: Root rot if the pot stays soggy.

plants.about: A smaller, tidier citrus that suits planters. The fruit can colour up before it is sweet, so always taste one first.
plants.name: Mandarin
plants.next: Summer feed of citrus food in December.
plants.petNote: Leaves and peel can upset cats and the dog. A little fruit flesh is fine for the birds.
plants.watch: Aphids on new growth and leaf miner trails.

plants.about: The Swiss cheese plant. Splits and holes appear as leaves mature, and its aerial roots help it climb.
plants.name: Monstera
plants.next: Give it a post or tree to climb.
plants.petNote: Irritates the mouth and throat if chewed.
plants.watch: Yellow leaves mean too wet. Protect from frost.

plants.about: An evergreen with shallow roots that hate drying out or being dug around. Fruit holds well on the tree, so pick as you need it.
plants.feed: Citrus food Sep, Dec and Mar
plants.name: Orange
plants.next: Summer feed of citrus food in December.
plants.petNote: Leaves and peel can upset cats and the dog. A little fruit flesh is fine for the birds.
plants.watch: Yellowing leaves (hungry), scale, and silver trails from leaf miner.

plants.about: A slow, graceful indoor palm that copes with lower light. Each stem only makes a few new fronds a year.
plants.name: Parlour palm
plants.next: Repot in spring if roots circle the pot.
plants.petNote: Safe for all your pets.
plants.watch: Fine webbing from spider mites, and brown tips.

plants.about: A forgiving indoor plant that tells you when it is thirsty: the leaves flop, then perk up within hours of a drink.
plants.name: Peace lily
plants.next: Wipe the leaves clean once a month.
plants.petNote: Irritates the mouth and throat. Painful but rarely serious. Keep it away from the birds' perch.
plants.watch: Brown leaf tips (dry air). Toxic to cats and dogs.

plants.about: A deciduous stone fruit. It fruits on last summer’s growth, so a light prune straight after harvest keeps it cropping well next year.
plants.name: Peach
plants.next: Bird netting goes on in December.
plants.petNote: Fruit is fine, but leaves, stones and seeds are toxic. Clear up fallen fruit.
plants.watch: Leaf curl (red, puckered leaves) in spring, and birds as soon as the fruit colours.
plants.water: Deep soak weekly; twice in heat

plants.about: A tough, bushy small tree with glossy leaves and bright orange-red flowers in summer. Fruit is ready when the skin turns deep red and sounds hollow when tapped.
plants.name: Pomegranate
plants.next: Watch for the first orange-red flowers.
plants.petNote: The seeds are a good cockatiel treat in small amounts. Peel and bark can upset cats and the dog.
plants.watch: Fruit splitting after heavy rain following a dry spell; keep watering even.
plants.water: Deep weekly; less once fruit sets

plants.about: Its centre blushes red when it's about to flower. After flowering it slowly fades and makes pups you can pot up.
plants.feed: Weak liquid feed monthly in summer
plants.name: Red bromeliad
plants.next: Look for pups at the base after flowering.
plants.petNote: Safe for all your pets.
plants.watch: Stagnant water in the cup; flush it out every couple of weeks.
plants.water: Keep the centre cup topped up

plants.about: Grown for its glossy burgundy leaves. Brighter light gives deeper colour, but harsh sun scorches it.
plants.name: Red cordyline
plants.next: Trim off old lower leaves to show the stem.
plants.petNote: Can cause vomiting, especially in cats.
plants.watch: Brown leaf tips and mealybugs.

plants.about: Not a true palm but an ancient cycad. It pushes out one flush of stiff, glossy fronds a year, so be patient.
plants.name: Sago palms
plants.next: Leave new soft fronds alone until they harden.
plants.petNote: Very toxic: even a small chew can cause liver failure. Keep it out of reach, and call your vet straight away if it's chewed.
plants.spot: Pink pot, 2 grey planters at the front, back bed (4)
plants.watch: Scale insects. Every part is very toxic to pets.

plants.about: Year-old plants are at their peak. They send out runners in summer that you can pot up for free new plants.
plants.name: Strawberries
plants.next: Peak picking, then pot up the best runners.
plants.petNote: Safe. Berries make a nice treat for the cockatiels. Use pet-safe slug control only.
plants.spot: Two black planters by the house
plants.watch: Slugs at night, birds, and grey mould on fruit in wet weather.

plants.about: Glossy leaflets fan out like the spokes of an umbrella. It leans toward the light, so regular turning keeps it straight.
plants.name: Umbrella trees
plants.next: Pinch the tips to keep it bushy.
plants.petNote: Irritates the mouth and throat if chewed. Keep it away from the birds.
plants.spot: Indoor basket, patio (leggy variegated dwarf) and front yard
plants.watch: Sudden leaf drop (draughts or overwatering) and scale.

plants.name: Lemon
plants.about: A big, productive lemon, flowering now. Lemons crop on and off all year in Auckland.
plants.watch: Yellow, blotchy leaves right now: usually low magnesium.
plants.next: Feed now: citrus food plus 1 tbsp Epsom salts in 10 L water.
plants.petNote: Leaves and peel can upset cats and the dog.

plants.name: Guava
plants.spot: Back corner by the chain fence
plants.about: A subtropical tree with strongly veined leaves. Purple older leaves in spring usually mean cold nights.
plants.watch: Purple-tinged leaves (cold or low phosphorus); guava moth in the fruit.
plants.next: Feed lightly as it warms up.
plants.petNote: Believed safe for all your pets.

plants.name: Chillies
plants.spot: Side veggie bed by the house
plants.about: A bushy chilli already flowering. More sun and warmth means hotter chillies.
plants.watch: A few yellow leaves: feed it, and check for aphids.
plants.next: Feed fortnightly now that it is flowering.
plants.petNote: Hot chillies burn mouths and eyes; leaves can upset tummies.

plants.name: Capsicum
plants.spot: Side veggie bed by the house
plants.about: Sweet peppers start green and ripen to red, yellow or orange. Patience gives sweeter fruit.
plants.watch: Aphids under the leaves; flower drop in cold nights.
plants.next: Stake it once fruit forms.
plants.petNote: Leaves and stems can upset tummies; ripe fruit is fine.

plants.name: Tomatoes
plants.water: Deep, every 2–3 days at the base
plants.feed: Tomato food every 2 weeks once flowering
plants.about: Eight young staked plants growing fast. Tying them in and pinching side shoots keeps them tidy and fruitful.
plants.watch: Blight in humid weather, whitefly, and weeds crowding the base.
plants.next: Pinch out side shoots and tie to stakes each week.
plants.petNote: Leaves, stems and green fruit are toxic; ripe tomatoes are fine.

plants.name: Eggplant
plants.spot: Side veggie bed, by the blue frog
plants.about: Already flowering with its pretty purple flowers. It loves heat, so a warm summer means a good crop.
plants.watch: Holes from slugs and flea beetles in the leaves.
plants.next: Feed fortnightly while flowering.
plants.petNote: Leaves and green fruit are toxic to pets.

plants.name: Silverbeet
plants.about: Big, crinkly leaves with white stems. Pick the outer leaves and it keeps producing for months.
plants.watch: Slugs, and leaf miner trails in the leaves.
plants.next: Keep picking outer leaves every week.
plants.petNote: Fine in small amounts; high in oxalates.

plants.name: Bok choy
plants.about: Young seedlings under the netting. Bok choy grows fast and is ready in about 6 weeks.
plants.watch: Cabbage white caterpillars, and bolting (going to seed) in hot weather.
plants.next: Keep the netting on; water often.
plants.petNote: Safe for all your pets.

plants.name: Bele
plants.spot: Black pot by the window (a cutting)
plants.feed: Liquid feed every 2 weeks once growing
plants.about: Pacific island cabbage. The young leaves are cooked like spinach. This one is a cutting, still rooting.
plants.watch: Snails and slugs love it; it drops leaves below about 10°C.
plants.next: Watch for new leaves at the buds in 2–4 weeks.
plants.petNote: Leaves are eaten by people; can upset a dog's stomach in quantity.

plants.name: Beans
plants.spot: Side bed along the chain-link fence
plants.about: A row of young climbing beans that will use the chain-link fence as a trellis. Pick often to keep them coming.
plants.watch: Slugs on seedlings; weeds in the row.
plants.next: Guide the vines onto the fence as they climb.
plants.petNote: Raw beans are toxic to birds; cook them before sharing.

plants.name: Bitter melon
plants.spot: Black pot on the trellis by the window
plants.about: Karela, climbing the window trellis. It loves heat and makes warty fruit that is picked green.
plants.watch: Snails in the pot (seen in your photo) and weeds crowding it.
plants.next: Weed the pot and tie the vine onto the trellis.
plants.petNote: Fruit and seeds are unsafe for birds; can upset cats and the dog.

plants.name: Taro
plants.spot: Side bed by the chain-link fence (about 15)
plants.about: Big heart-shaped leaves on purple stems. Both leaves and corms must be cooked well before eating.
plants.watch: Old leaves yellowing is normal; snails chew holes in new leaves.
plants.next: Remove yellow leaves and keep the bed moist.
plants.petNote: Raw leaves and corms burn the mouth and throat of pets.

plants.name: Basil
plants.about: Sweet basil, growing in the veggie bed. Pinching the tips makes it bushy.
plants.watch: Flowers forming: pinch them off to keep leaves coming.
plants.next: Pinch the tips to make it bushier.
plants.petNote: Safe for all your pets.

plants.name: Mint
plants.about: Spreads fast, so it is best kept in pots, as you have it. Cut it back hard to get fresh leaves.
plants.watch: Rust (orange spots); cut affected stems right back.
plants.next: Cut back by half for fresh growth.
plants.petNote: Large amounts can upset cats and the dog; fine for the birds.

plants.name: White & pink rose
plants.about: Creamy white petals edged in pink. It repeat-flowers all summer with deadheading.
plants.watch: Black spot and yellow leaves, and weeds in the pot.
plants.next: Deadhead after each flush.
plants.petNote: Safe, apart from the thorns.

plants.name: Pink rose
plants.about: A bright pink rose. Good air flow around it is the best defence against black spot.
plants.watch: Black spot; aphids on new buds.
plants.next: Deadhead after each flush.
plants.petNote: Safe, apart from the thorns.

plants.name: Orange rose
plants.about: A warm orange rose that glows in evening light.
plants.watch: Black spot on lower leaves.
plants.next: Deadhead after each flush.
plants.petNote: Safe, apart from the thorns.

plants.name: Peach rose
plants.about: Soft peach blooms that fade paler as they open.
plants.watch: Black spot and yellowing leaves.
plants.next: Deadhead after each flush.
plants.petNote: Safe, apart from the thorns.

plants.name: Stargazer lilies
plants.about: Big, scented pink flowers with dark speckles. They come back from the bulb every summer.
plants.watch: Botrytis (brown spots) in wet weather.
plants.next: Move them out of the cats’ reach, or remove them.
plants.petNote: Deadly to cats: even pollen or vase water can cause kidney failure. Vet straight away.

plants.name: Gardenias
plants.about: Creamy, heavily scented flowers. Gardenias need acid soil to keep their leaves green.
plants.watch: Yellow leaves with green veins right now: needs acid food and iron.
plants.next: Feed with azalea or gardenia food.
plants.petNote: Can upset tummies if chewed.

plants.name: Hibiscus
plants.about: Cut right back over winter. It should reshoot strongly as the weather warms.
plants.watch: Mostly yellow leaves now; aphids and mealybugs on new shoots.
plants.next: Feed once new shoots appear.
plants.petNote: Generally safe; can upset a dog's stomach.

plants.name: Mexican heather
plants.about: A neat little shrub covered in tiny pink-purple flowers for months.
plants.watch: Very little; trim if it gets leggy.
plants.next: Light trim after the first flush.
plants.petNote: Safe for all your pets.

plants.name: Periwinkle
plants.about: Cheerful pink flowers all summer, and very tough in heat.
plants.watch: Root rot if pots stay soggy.
plants.next: Move the pots up out of pets’ reach.
plants.petNote: Very toxic: vomiting, low blood pressure, even seizures.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum
plants.about: Flowers in autumn as days shorten. Pinch the tips until January for a bushier plant.
plants.watch: Aphids and leaf spot.
plants.next: Pinch tips until January.
plants.petNote: Can cause vomiting and drooling in cats and the dog.

plants.name: Moss rose
plants.about: Bright red flowers on fleshy, needle-like leaves. The flowers open in full sun.
plants.watch: Overwatering.
plants.next: Let it dry out between drinks.
plants.petNote: Can upset cats and the dog if chewed.

plants.name: Anthuriums
plants.spot: On the heat pump unit (2): move them
plants.about: Glossy red heart-shaped flowers that last for weeks.
plants.watch: Yellow, blotchy leaves: likely harsh sun, overwatering or the heat pump blast.
plants.next: Move off the heat pump into bright shade.
plants.petNote: Irritates the mouth and throat if chewed.

plants.name: Split-leaf philodendron
plants.about: Big, deeply cut leaves that make a tropical statement.
plants.watch: Yellow lower leaves (normal ageing or too wet).
plants.next: Remove yellow lower leaves.
plants.petNote: Irritates the mouth and throat if chewed.

plants.name: Rubber plant
plants.about: Glossy burgundy leaves with a red sheath on each new leaf.
plants.watch: Dusty leaves (wipe them) and leaf drop when moved.
plants.next: Wipe the leaves clean.
plants.petNote: The milky sap irritates skin and tummies.

plants.name: Weeping figs
plants.about: Green and variegated figs with small, glossy leaves. They sulk and drop leaves when moved.
plants.watch: Leaf drop after a move or a draught.
plants.next: Leave them in one spot.
plants.petNote: The milky sap irritates skin and tummies.

plants.name: Dragon trees
plants.spot: Deck (yellow-striped), patio red pot & urn (red-edged), shade house
plants.about: Spiky tufts of strappy leaves on slim canes. The red-edged ones colour best in bright light.
plants.watch: Brown tips from dry air or fluoride; lower leaves dropping is normal.
plants.next: Trim brown tips with clean scissors.
plants.petNote: Can cause vomiting, especially in cats.

plants.name: Variegated flax
plants.about: A New Zealand native with cream-striped sword leaves. Tui love the flowers.
plants.watch: Mealybugs deep in the leaf bases.
plants.next: Pull out dead leaves from the base.
plants.petNote: Safe for all your pets.

plants.name: Cabbage trees
plants.about: Tī kōuka, a New Zealand icon. Scented cream flowers in late spring.
plants.watch: Dead leaves hanging under the head; pull them off.
plants.next: Tidy away the dead leaves.
plants.petNote: Can upset tummies if chewed.

plants.name: Ferns
plants.about: Lacy fronds around the pond, unrolling from fiddleheads in spring.
plants.watch: Drying out in hot spells.
plants.next: Water in dry weather.
plants.petNote: Safe for all your pets.

plants.name: Variegated pittosporum
plants.about: A neat native shrub with cream-edged leaves. Trims well into a ball.
plants.watch: Scale insects on the stems.
plants.next: Light trim to keep it rounded.
plants.petNote: Safe for all your pets.

plants.name: Golden breath of heaven
plants.about: Soft, golden, fragrant foliage with tiny pink flowers in spring.
plants.watch: Root rot in soggy soil.
plants.next: Trim lightly after flowering.
plants.petNote: Not known to be toxic, but best not chewed.

plants.name: Bloodleaf
plants.about: Dark red leaves with pink veins. Pinching the tips keeps it bushy.
plants.watch: Leggy growth in shade.
plants.next: Pinch the tips.
plants.petNote: Safe for all your pets.

plants.name: Calathea
plants.spot: On the heat pump unit: move it
plants.about: Patterned leaves that fold up at night, a “prayer plant”.
plants.watch: Crispy edges from the heat pump air and dry air.
plants.next: Move off the heat pump into shade.
plants.petNote: Safe for all your pets.

plants.name: Stromanthe Triostar
plants.spot: On the heat pump unit: move it
plants.about: Leaves striped pink, cream and green, with pink undersides.
plants.watch: Crispy edges and faded colour from the heat pump blast.
plants.next: Move off the heat pump into bright shade.
plants.petNote: Safe for all your pets.

plants.name: Peperomia
plants.about: The baby rubber plant: thick, glossy, round leaves.
plants.watch: Yellow blotchy leaves: usually too much water.
plants.next: Let it dry out before watering.
plants.petNote: Safe for all your pets.

plants.name: Tradescantia
plants.about: Trailing stems of striped leaves. Snip pieces off and they root in water.
plants.watch: Leggy stems; pinch them back.
plants.next: Pinch back leggy stems.
plants.petNote: Sap can irritate skin and mouths.

plants.name: Elephant bush
plants.about: Like a mini jade with red stems and tiny round leaves. Edible, and very forgiving.
plants.watch: Rot if the soil stays wet.
plants.next: Leave it be.
plants.petNote: Safe for all your pets.

plants.name: Aloe
plants.about: Spiky, spotted rosettes. Many aloes flower in winter, which tui love.
plants.watch: Rot from wet soil; scale on the leaves.
plants.next: Move into more sun to stay compact.
plants.petNote: Causes vomiting and diarrhoea in cats and the dog.
Safe; the fruit is a good cockatiel treat in small amounts.
plants.name: Yellow cherry guava
plants.about: A glossy-leaved small tree with coppery new growth and fluffy white flowers, now in bud. The yellow fruit is sweeter and milder than the red.
plants.watch: Guava moth grubs in the fruit, and birds once it ripens. Pull up any seedlings, as it self-seeds easily.
plants.next: Flowering now; fruit sets over summer.

plants.petNote: Safe; the fruit is a good cockatiel treat in small amounts.
plants.name: Red cherry guava
plants.spot: Front waterfall, between the lime and feijoa
plants.about: The classic red cherry guava: glossy leaves, smooth peeling bark and tangy-sweet red fruit, lovely fresh or in jam.
plants.watch: Guava moth grubs in the fruit, and birds once it ripens. Pull up any seedlings, as it self-seeds easily.
plants.next: Flowering soon; fruit sets over summer.

week.headline: Lilies and slug pellets first: the cats come before anything else.
next: Peach: bird netting up before the fruit colours.
Citrus: summer feed coming early December.

tasks.text: Finish thinning: leave one fruit every 15 cm so the rest size up.
After Wednesday's rain, top up mulch to 5–8 cm while the planter is moist. Keep it off the trunk.
Thin to one apple per cluster; keep the biggest, best-shaped one.
Check the codling moth trap. Note how many moths are in it.
Skip watering mid-week if Wednesday brings the forecast rain. Finger-test again on the weekend.
Look under new leaves for aphids. Hose them off.
Top up mulch after the rain, clear of the trunk.
Windy mid-week: check stakes and ties after Wednesday.
Pick fruit as soon as it's fully red, every 2 days.
Wet weather brings slugs. Check at night or set beer traps.
Get netting over the plants before the weekend.
Raised planters dry fast once the sun returns: finger-test 5 cm deep on Saturday.
In flower now. Let the rain do the watering; water deeply if it turns dry.
Pick off the spotted, yellow leaves and bin them (not compost). Clear fallen ones too.
Pull the clover out of the planter so air can move around the base.
Pots dry quickly once it warms up: water every 2–3 days after the rain clears.
Snip off spent flower heads to keep new ones coming.
No water needed this week; the rain is plenty.
Water when the leaves start to droop; wipe the dust off the leaves.
Keep it in bright light but out of direct sun; wipe dusty fronds.
Pull the dandelions and grass out of the pink pot (wear gloves).
Give a liquid feed now it's growing again.
Turn the basket a quarter so it grows evenly.
Move it out of hot sun and trim off the yellow, scorched leaves.
Pull the grass out of the pot.
Keep the cuttings out of heavy rain on Wednesday; light mist only after.

alerts.title: Stargazer lilies near the cats
alerts.text: Lilies are deadly to cats: a little pollen licked off fur or a sip of vase water can cause kidney failure.
alerts.action: Move them where the cats can’t go, or remove them. Vet straight away if a cat has pollen on it.

alerts.title: Check the slug pellets in every bed
alerts.text: Pellets are scattered through the veggie beds, pots and pomegranate bed, next to a pet water bowl.
alerts.action: Check the box: iron phosphate (e.g. Quash) is fine; metaldehyde (e.g. Blitzem) must be cleared up and binned.

alerts.title: Sago palm within reach of pets
alerts.text: It's the most dangerous plant in the garden: even a small chew can cause liver failure in cats, dogs and birds.
alerts.action: Move the pink pot where the cats, dog and cockatiels can't reach it. Wear gloves when you weed it.

alerts.title: Black spot on the coral rose
alerts.text: Dark spots and yellowing leaves are showing, and rain spreads the spores.
alerts.action: Pick off spotted leaves and clear fallen ones. Bin them, don't compost them.

alerts.title: Dracaena scorching in the sun
alerts.text: The striped leaves have yellow, bleached patches from hot sun on the patio.
alerts.action: Move the pot into shade, such as the shade house, and trim off the worst leaves.

alerts.title: A front-bed succulent is shrivelling
alerts.text: One near the front edge has gone yellow and dry.
alerts.action: Check it isn't sitting wet under the bark. If it's mushy, pull it and plant a fresh cutting.

alerts.title: Weeds taking over the patio pots
alerts.text: Grass and dandelions are growing in the jade and sago pots, competing for water.
alerts.action: Pull them out this week (gloves on for the sago).

alerts.title: Showery, windy spells this week
alerts.text: Heavy showers can rot young cuttings, and gusts can rock young trees.
alerts.action: Move the cuttings table under cover, and check ties on the citrus and pomegranate.

alerts.title: Birds will find the peaches
alerts.text: As the fruit starts colouring in December, birds move in fast.
alerts.action: Have bird netting ready to go on by early December.

alerts.title: Grey mould and slugs on berries
alerts.text: Damp weather plus ripe fruit is when mould and slugs strike.
alerts.action: Pick every 2 days, remove any mouldy fruit, and use pet-safe slug control.

alerts.title: Indoor plants near the cockatiels
alerts.text: Peace lilies and the umbrella tree irritate the mouth if the birds nibble them.
alerts.action: Keep them away from where the cockatiels perch or play out of the cage.

alerts.title: Pots drying out as summer arrives
alerts.text: Hydrangeas, palms in crates and planters dry fast on the first hot days.
alerts.action: Water deeply in the morning and check pots every 2–3 days.

alerts.title: Guava moth season ahead
alerts.text: Guava moth grubs can ruin feijoas from the inside.
alerts.action: Hang a guava moth trap in the tree in December.

alerts.title: Plants sitting on the heat pump
alerts.text: The anthuriums, calathea, stromanthe and corn plant are crisping in its hot and cold blasts.
alerts.action: Move them off the unit into bright shade nearby.

alerts.title: Yellow blotchy citrus leaves
alerts.text: The lemon and mandarin show yellow between the veins: low magnesium.
alerts.action: Feed with citrus food plus 1 tbsp Epsom salts in 10 L water.

alerts.title: Curled, browned apple tips
alerts.text: Twisted leaves at the tips usually mean aphids or leaf roller caterpillars.
alerts.action: Uncurl a few leaves; squash or hose off what you find.

alerts.title: Gardenias yellowing
alerts.text: Yellow leaves with green veins mean they need more acid.
alerts.action: Feed with azalea or gardenia food.

alerts.title: Periwinkle at pet height
alerts.text: Several pots on the deck and in the shade house are very toxic to pets.
alerts.action: Lift them onto shelves or move them where the pets don’t go.

alerts.title: Weeds racing the veggies
alerts.text: Lots of weed seedlings are coming up between the tomatoes, peppers and around the pomegranate.
alerts.action: A quick hoe while they’re tiny saves a lot of work later.
